title: A lens over lenses: what a colour lens is, built once

Today a lens reads other lenses' tables (reads); reading their focus is the step. Its word - filter is the candidate - to be found in the making. More meanings to come as lenses need them: a state, a warning, a link, a date. Parked 2026-11-12 by the author, against his own idea: I do not see what a colour lens clarifies - it would drift meaning from the actual data into someone's head, of what someone thinks is beautiful or more important, without reflecting in the ecosystem, blurring the meanings of dome and surfaces. title: ocoeco's reading of what is typed dissolves into argenv's reader; what fits here is the lens asked the other way
note: The commons' rule is a declared command line (argenv). ocoeco still uses clap; the entries of lenses are checked for collisions by the build script. When ocoeco moves to argenv, each entry's flags become part of the declared contract. 2026-11-13: the most valuable of the five to move. Lens entries are taken before the parser by hand, because the older library could not take what lenses declare; with argenv a build step makes the declarations from the lens files, so entries are real commands with help, completions and man pages, and a collision is the compiler's to find. 2026-11-13, looked at what argenv carries: typed inputs (text, yes or no, one of a set, a list, numbers, a path), options that repeat, positionals, inputs scoped to one command, and usage and a schema made from the one declaration. Nothing ocoeco needs is missing for the move; only offering the id of an existing row waits on argenv's own open item (a list known only at runtime). The author has set this first: the fulldome's form tells how to use it from a legend typed by hand - a program dictating its use from behind brackets. 2026-11-13, set right: it was said here that nothing ocoeco needs is missing in argenv. That was read off the names of its fields, not tried. Tried: a repeated option with free values, and more positionals than are named, cannot be declared. The need is met in argenv, where it lives, before ocoeco moves. 2026-11-13, the trial (a throwaway program, nothing changed in either repository): the item entry of the work lens, turned into records as the program runs, was read by argenv's own reader as it is. Eight typed lines: what was given was read, with the door each value came through (who is driving came from the environment - what the computer supplies and argenv's second door are one thing); a misspelt word was answered with what was meant; a value outside the set was refused with the set, taken from the lens; a missing id and a missing value were named. Three signs: needed is not one thing (a title is needed for a new row, not for a change - known only from what exists, and a record can only say always); the reader cannot say a link points nowhere (what a relation knows has nowhere to go in a record); and it reads what was typed but does not say what could be. So it no longer waits on argenv: nothing in argenv had to change. 2026-11-13: done for entries - a typed line is read back by argenv's reader (decision 2026-11-13-a-surface-reads-back); ocoeco's own reader of typed words is retired. 2026-11-13: the reader speaks for itself - what it could not take is said in argenv's own words, with only what the entry knows added (what it asks). The lines that restated its findings in ocoeco's earlier wording are gone: they had been kept for a test's sentence.

With them, from elsewhere: asking the lab, waiting for a job with its end told by the exit status, and standing in the lab's record as it arrived - all with the commons' own programs. 2026-11-13: the release path is in place (decision 2026-11-13-ocoeco-is-released-as-files); a workflow may now open a pull request in this repository, as in tad's - it could not, the same thing found in the phone's docs on 12 November. 2026-11-13: the path is on main and its first run failed, as it must until then: GitHub answered that the organisation does not allow Actions to create or approve pull requests, so the repository's own setting cannot be changed (asked twice; refused with that reason). Left failing and not switched off: it shows while it is true and stops by itself when the setting allows it - switching it off would be a thing to remember to switch back on. Not changed by the driver: it widens what workflows may do across the organisation, which is its owner's to decide. 2026-11-13: the organisation now allows workflows to open pull requests (the author's word); the release pull request was opened and merged, ocoeco-v0.2.0 tagged, and the conveyor built the program and its .deb - then the .rpm step looked for ocoeco/Cargo.toml: the tool takes -p as a folder, which is where tad's package lives and not where ocoeco's does. tad's script with the name changed was untrue in one word; and only the build had been run before landing, not the packing. Both are now run on the lab as the conveyor runs them. 2026-11-13, done: ocoeco-v0.2.1 carries eight files - a tarball, a .deb and an .rpm for x86_64 and aarch64, with their checksums. Taken from the public release on a machine that had never built it, checked against its checksum, it ran, and the lens of language was looked through there: the same ten lenses, 25 tables, 166 fields as on the lab. ocoeco-v0.2.0 carries no files, and says so on itself.
